description: Toy Box Friends G5-01: adding and subtracting fractions with unlike denominators at Monkey's smoothie shack. 1/2 + 1/3 is not 2/5: rename to a common denominator first.

youtube.title: Adding Fractions with Unlike Denominators | Common Denominators | Grade 5 Math | Toy Box Friends
youtube.description:
Monkey says 1/2 cup + 1/3 cup = 2/5 cup. But that's less than the banana alone! Robo shows why we can only add pieces of the same size: rename the fractions with a common denominator, add the numerators and keep the denominator.
You'll learn: why 1/2 + 1/3 is not 2/5, how to find a common denominator with lists of multiples, how to estimate with benchmark fractions (0, 1/2, 1), subtracting fractions, and answers greater than one (mixed numbers).
Try at home with a grown-up: use measuring cups and water on a tray. Estimate first, then pour 1/2 cup and 1/3 cup into a 1-cup measure. Wipe up spills so nobody slips.

objects.text: Order 1: 1/2 cup yoghurt and 1/4 cup berries. How much in all?
Order 2: 1/3 cup mango, 1/2 cup banana and 1/6 cup oats.
Bear walks 5/6 km of beach. He has walked 1/2 km. How far is left?

1. Estimate first.
2. Find a common denominator.
3. Rename the fractions.
4. Add or subtract the numerators.
5. Keep the denominator. Simplify.

do.text: Adding Fractions with Unlike Denominators
Welcome to Monkey's Smoothie Shack! Today's special: banana mango!
One half cup of banana...
...plus one third cup of mango.
Top plus top, bottom plus bottom. Two fifths of a cup. Easy!
Hmm. Let me pour two fifths of a cup.
Look. The whole smoothie is smaller than the banana alone!
Monkey, how can that be?
What do you think? Can the answer be two fifths?
Let's check with fraction bars. Every bar is the same whole: one cup.
This bar shows one half. That's the banana.
This one shows one third. That's the mango.
And here's my two fifths!
Compare the shaded parts. Two fifths is shorter than one half.
But adding mango should make the smoothie bigger, not smaller.
Oops! So my answer can't be right.
The bottom number is the denominator. It names the size of the pieces.
denominator
The top number is the numerator. It counts how many pieces.
numerator
Halves are big pieces. Thirds are smaller pieces.
We can't add different-sized pieces as they are.
One meter plus one centimeter isn't two meter-centimeters!
1 m + 1 cm is not 2 "m-cm"
Fun fact: in North Africa, mathematicians like al-Hassar
fun fact
wrote fractions with a line between the numbers, over eight hundred years ago.
Now estimate. One half plus a bit more is more than one half.
And one third is less than one half, so the total is less than one whole.
between 1/2 and 1
Here's the trick. We slice the pieces until they're all the same size.
Slice each half into three. Now there are six pieces: sixths.
Three of the six pieces are shaded. One half equals three sixths.
Now slice each third into two. That makes sixths too.
One third equals two sixths.
Same-size pieces? Then they stack together.
Three sixths plus two sixths is five sixths.
The numerators add: three plus two is five.
The denominator stays six, because the piece size did not change.
the denominator stays the same
Let's check on a number line cut into sixths.
Three sixths of banana...
...and two more sixths of mango!
Five sixths. More than half, less than one whole. Just like our estimate.
Let's pour it all into one cup.
Five sixths of a cup. Almost full, but not quite!
How did we know to use sixths? We look for a common denominator.
common denominator
List the multiples of each denominator. Multiples of two:
Multiples of three:
Which number is in both lists first?
Six! It's in both lists!
Yes. Six is a common multiple, so sixths work for halves and thirds.
Now a new one: one fourth plus one sixth.
Multiples of four: four, eight, twelve. Multiples of six: six, twelve.
What's the common denominator?
Twelve!
Right. Cut both bars into twelfths.
One fourth is three twelfths.
One sixth is two twelfths.
Three twelfths plus two twelfths is five twelfths.
Could I just multiply the denominators? Four times six is twenty-four.
That works too! Six twenty-fourths plus four twenty-fourths is ten twenty-fourths.
Ten twenty-fourths simplifies to five twelfths. Same answer, just smaller pieces.
Fun fact: ancient Egyptians had a special symbol just for two thirds.
fun fact
Before the exact answer, estimate with benchmarks: zero, one half and one.
benchmark
One half plus three eighths.
Three eighths is a bit less than a half. So the total is a bit less than one.
I got four tenths!
Four tenths is less than one half. It's even smaller than the first part!
My estimate caught my mistake! I forgot to rename.
One half is four eighths. Four eighths plus three eighths is seven eighths.
Now two thirds plus one half. Is it more or less than one?
More! Two thirds plus one half goes past one.
Is it three fifths?
Three fifths is less than two thirds. Impossible! Rename to sixths.
Four sixths plus three sixths is seven sixths. That's more than one, as we estimated.
Hello! May I have some juice, please?
I have three fourths of a cup. I'll pour one third of a cup for you, Bear.
How much juice is left for Monkey? Three fourths minus one third.
Different denominators again. What's the common denominator for four and three?
Twelve! Three fourths is nine twelfths, and one third is four twelfths.
Take away four twelfths.
Nine twelfths minus four twelfths is five twelfths.
On the number line: start at nine twelfths and leap back four.
Five twelfths left for Monkey, and a nice cup for me!
Two thirds plus three fourths. Estimate first: more or less than one?
More! Both parts are more than a half.
Rename with twelfths: eight twelfths plus nine twelfths is seventeen twelfths.
Twelve twelfths fill one whole circle.
Five more twelfths start the next one.
Seventeen twelfths is one whole and five twelfths. We call that a mixed number.
mixed number
One and five twelfths cups! I need a bigger blender.
Rename, add the numerators, keep the denominator
Same-size pieces?
Then add the tops!
The bottom?
Stays the same!
Rename, then add, the bottom stays! Same-size pieces every day!
Smoothie rush! I have three orders. Can you work them out?
Order one: one half cup of yoghurt and one quarter cup of berries. How much in all?
One half is two quarters. Two quarters plus one quarter is three quarters of a cup.
Three quarters. Perfect!
Order two: one third mango, one half banana and one sixth oats.
Sixths work for all three: two sixths plus three sixths plus one sixth.
Six sixths. That's exactly one cup!
Order three is about me. I walk five sixths of a kilometer on the beach.
I've walked one half of a kilometer so far. How far is left?
Five sixths minus three sixths is two sixths, which is one third of a kilometer.
Only one third of a kilometer to go. Thank you!
Question one. Why is one half plus one third not two fifths?
Two fifths is less than one half. The pieces were different sizes.
Question two. What is one half plus one fourth?
Three fourths!
Question three. What is five sixths minus one third?
Five sixths minus two sixths is three sixths, which is one half.
Question four. Is three fourths plus two thirds more or less than one?
More! It's seventeen twelfths: one and five twelfths.
Let's recap the steps.
Estimate first. Find a common denominator. Rename the fractions.
Add or subtract the numerators, keep the denominator, and simplify.
And here's a perfect five sixths cup smoothie for Bear!
Mmm. Delicious maths!
Your turn! With a grown-up, use measuring cups and water on a tray.
with a grown-up
Estimate first: will one half cup plus one third cup fill one cup? Then pour and see.
Wipe up spills so nobody slips. See you next time!
